name: Anlatım ve telaffuz

local_gate.web_gates: not re-run: this batch changed no web source (B20's run stands)

blocked_on_the_desktop.status: READY_FOR_OWNER - needs an idle desktop, not a code change
blocked_on_the_desktop.why: The operator lab drives the REAL desktop: it launches Notepad, activates it, clicks inside it and reads `Registry.Foreground()` microseconds later. This batch changed no device code at all (`git status devices/` is empty), and the same suite passed three times earlier today. It began failing when the desktop became busy: first the foreground was taken by a window titled "Claude" (this session's own client raising itself), and then - with the owner watching a full-screen video - by something the registry could not resolve at all.
blocked_on_the_desktop.what_changed_here: Only the diagnosis. The failure used to read `Assert.Equal() Failure: Strings differ / w-3802978-342479328 / w-5834690-342479218`, which names neither party. It now names the intruder and the remedy: "after 3 attempt(s) the click landed while the foreground was <title> [<image>]; the operator lab needs a desktop nobody else is using".
not_done_on_purpose: The assertion was NOT loosened: 'the click landed in OUR window' is the claim that separates an operator from a keylogger, and `pointer.click` captures the foreground immediately after synthesising the click, so the claim is fair.

The retry count was NOT raised: this file's own comment rejects widening a bound that keeps losing, and three activations that each verified `foreground: true` were already enough to prove the desktop is being taken back.
`PAGENTOS_OPERATOR_LAB=0` was NOT set. Disabling the lab to make a gate green is the move this repository exists to avoid; the switch is the owner's.

The stray Notepad on the desktop was NOT closed: its title is `*a.txt`, the asterisk means unsaved work, and it has been open since 2026-09-10. It is the owner's document and it is not the cause (it never held the foreground in any observed failure).
blocked_on_the_desktop.rest_of_the_suite: 919 of 920 agent tests and 135 of 135 audio tests pass.

what_this_proves: The narration subsystem makes a sound, and the assistant says the owner's words the way the owner says them. A command that positions the cursor now returns audio a client can play, with the next sentences already synthesised; the pronunciation table can be filled by speaking and reaches the assistant's OWN speech; and four things Turkish does with the characters around a number are now read correctly.
the_shape_of_this_batch: The oldest shape in this repository, at its largest. `app/narration/engine.py` has planned, split, cached, looked ahead and cancelled since M4 — and its `Synthesizer` seam had NO implementation anywhere under `app/`. The only thing that ever passed one was a test. Sixteen hundred lines of narration machinery, a REST surface, a Turkish command machine, a cross-device cursor: complete, correct, and mute. Requirement 228's dictionary is the same story told with a different ending — a complete subsystem with one writer nobody could reach (a hand-made PUT), and therefore zero rows in production.

closed_fully.224_the_seam_has_something_behind_it: `ProviderSynthesizer` translates the engine's `synthesize(text, settings) -> bytes` onto every TTS provider's `synthesize(text, *, voice, speed, fmt) -> TTSResult` — the mismatch the matrix names. `build_synthesizer` returns **None** when the deployment has no provider that speaks, because B13 req 267 and B20 req 234 settled what the offline fake produces: a 110 Hz tone, and narration is the longest form of speech this system has and the least forgiving place to hum for ninety seconds.
closed_fully.225_226_the_queue_and_the_read_ahead_hav: `NarrationEngine.ensure_ahead` synthesises the cursor's chunk plus `NARRATION_LOOKAHEAD` more and cancels what the cursor moved away from. The command response names the chunks that are ready (`ready_ahead`) rather than claiming a read-ahead, and the test counts PROVIDER CALLS to prove the cache is what makes the second command instant.
closed_fully.227_a_paused_session_pays_for_nothing: "dur" is the one command that must never cost a provider call: the owner just said stop, and synthesising the next three sentences anyway is both money and the audio equivalent of not listening. The audio block is built only for a state the command machine itself calls READING.
closed_fully.414_an_artifact_can_be_asked_for: Narration had exactly one way to begin — `activity.explain` builds a briefing and attaches a session to it — so every other artifact could be opened on a screen and never read. `narration.start` takes an artifact id from `artifact.list` (an id, never a guessed title: reading the wrong document for two minutes is a worse failure than asking which one) and attaches the same durable narration every later command drives.
closed_fully.228_the_dictionary_can_be_filled_by_spea: The moment a pronunciation rule is worth writing is the moment the word came out wrong, and that moment is spoken. `pronunciation.teach` upserts (teaching the same word twice is a correction, not a second rule), `pronunciation.list` reads the table back, and `pronunciation.forget` takes an id from that list.
closed_fully.229_the_assistant_obeys_its_own_table: The dictionary reached two things: the narration plan's text, and what a tool handed back — both of them the assistant reading something PREPARED. What it said in its own words went to the provider having never seen the table. `pronunciation_block` puts the rules in the session instruction, bounded to 24 rules and 700 characters, worded as a rule about SPEAKING rather than spelling.
closed_fully.230_what_turkish_does_around_a_number: Four gaps, each found by reading a corpus out loud rather than by reading the code. The apostrophe ('1.000'den' → 'bin'den'), where joining alone is not enough because the author harmonised the suffix to the DIGITS and the preceding word has changed ('20:00'de' wants 'sıfırda'). The minus sign, which `cardinal()` has handled since M4 and no rule ever handed it one. The degree symbol, dropped silently in a system that reads a temperature every morning. And the solidus.
closed_fully.237_teknik_anlat_changes_the_reading: The presentation level reached the speech BUDGET and stopped there. The normaliser's technical mode — dotted runs as octets, no magnitude collapsing — is exactly what somebody asking for the technical version wants to hear, and no owner utterance could select it: `mode` came from the request body of a REST call the voice path does not make.

found_on_the_way.the_relay_refuses_the_obvious_argument_n: `pronunciation.teach` was written with `token` and `context`. `FORBIDDEN_KEY_PARTS` refuses both — `token` is credential-shaped, and `context` CONTAINS `text` — so the tool could never have been called, and it would have looked perfectly correct in review. Caught by `test_no_tool_schema_names_an_argument_the_relay_refuses`, which is the guard doing precisely its job; the arguments are now `written_form` and `scope`, and a test in this batch states the reason.
found_on_the_way.every_registered_tool_needs_a_tier: `test_every_registered_tool_has_a_tier` failed the moment the three tools existed. The map is complete in BOTH directions on purpose, and a default of OPEN is how a tool added later ends up ungoverned with nobody deciding it should be.
found_on_the_way.the_fake_is_refused_by_the_policy_it_ear: B20 made the tone policy ask the class, so `FakeTTSProvider` is refused by the narration path — correct in production and useless for exercising the path where audio IS produced. The tests use the explicit `synthetic_speech=False` stand-in, which `test_no_production_path_declares_a_fake_to_be_real_speech` forbids under `app/`.
found_on_the_way.1_2_is_not_ikide_bir: The mechanical fraction reading of '1/2' is 'ikide bir', which is a different Turkish EXPRESSION ('every so often'). It is one of two idioms the rule hard-codes; the other is '7/24'.

tests.services/api/tests/unit/test_voice_realt: +4 (229 end to end, 237, 414 and its refusal)

red_first_proof.method: Each claim was proved by an executed mutation of the production source, restored afterwards from a sha256-verified backup.
mutations: narration: return no audio on a reading command -> four audio tests fail; let `build_synthesizer` accept a tone provider -> the no-voice test fails.
pronunciation: stop passing the table to `_session_config` -> the end-to-end 229 test fails.
numbers: drop the apostrophe stage -> 8 fail; join without harmony -> 2 fail (the two the author's spelling gets wrong); disable the degree and sign stages -> 8 fail.
237: make `_narration_mode` always answer 'narration' -> the technical-reading test fails.
414: create the narration and never attach it -> the read-aloud test fails.

runtime_proof.why: REAL_PROOF_REQUIRED for 224/414 is real audio bytes from a real provider on a long text, and this deployment has no TTS credit — the roadmap's own allowance for that case is PROVEN_PROXY plus a BLOCKED note. What is proven: a real WAV, produced through the real engine and the real routes by a provider that returns bytes, fetched over the real HTTP surface, with its sha256 and its measured duration matching. The moment a key exists, `build_synthesizer` returns a real synthesizer through the same path and nothing else changes.

owner_gates.281_tts_credit: a TTS provider credit turns 224/414 from PROVEN_AUTOMATED into PROVEN_REAL; until then narration answers with text and says why
